primary_source_findings.finding: Brain2Qwerty v2 reports substantial inter-subject variability and identifies cross-subject transfer or self-supervised pretraining as a priority.
primary_source_findings.design_consequence: Use a separate development person before spending the final-only S25 verdict.

primary_source_findings.finding: Brain2Qwerty v2 assigns all instances of the same sentence text to one deterministic hash partition across subjects.
primary_source_findings.design_consequence: Future S24 selection text must be grouped and matching S21 source-train text excluded from fit.

primary_source_findings.finding: The Brain2Qwerty v2 auto-research protocol kept agents on validation and performed cross-subject evaluation once after tuning.
primary_source_findings.design_consequence: S24 is development-only; S25 remains the one-time final-person test.

primary_source_findings.finding: Brain2Qwerty v2 reports that both recording quantity and sentence diversity affect asynchronous encoder CER.
primary_source_findings.design_consequence: Report usable unique sentence groups, not merely duplicated row count.

primary_source_findings.finding: The official SpanishBCBL card declares the CC BY-NC 4.0 license, nominal MEG system, repeated-person aliases, and S23 exclusion.
primary_source_findings.design_consequence: Prefer clean S24 identity, preserve noncommercial posture, canonicalize aliases, and exclude S23.

primary_source_findings.finding: Primary methodological literature warns that tuning and reporting on the same validation evidence biases performance estimates and that small neuroimaging samples have large uncertainty.
primary_source_findings.design_consequence: Use S24 only for development, consume its selection rows after use, keep S25 independent, and never treat the 48-row floor as a power claim.

primary_source_findings.finding: Brain2Qwerty v2 states that its current whole-sentence architecture is noncausal and necessarily slow for word-by-word feedback.
primary_source_findings.design_consequence: A Loop 49 intake cannot support a real-time or home-device claim.
